title: One file a probe run wrote
description: Validated on read, at the node boundary. A malformed payload is the input to every downstream decision and would otherwise fail silently. A probe that dies partway leaves fewer of these, not broken ones.

pageComponents.description: Every custom element on the page, written when `within` matched nothing. It answers the question the wrong scope guess was asking, and unlike a page-wide walk it does not truncate.

droppedExchanges.description: How many exchanges the browser saw past its cap and did not record. Reported rather than silent, for the reason bodyDropped is: an absent exchange is otherwise indistinguishable from a call the application never made.

requests.description: Network exchanges the probe watched. Ticket 02's rule 3 says a fabricated response body must derive from a response the probe actually observed, and this is where the observation lives. Without it every stub would be invented from nothing.

bodyDropped.description: The body was over the cap and was dropped whole. Never clipped: a truncated JSON document that still parses anchors a stub to a fiction that looks observed.

attrs.description: The ladder's vocabulary only. The browser never sends another, which is how the ban list is enforced rather than merely documented.

allOf.comment: `nodes` is required of the two DOM kinds and of neither network payload. It used to be required of every payload, which is the whole reason this clause exists rather than the flat `required` list.
